blocks.content: Natural vegetation refers to plant life that grows without human aid and remains largely undisturbed by human activity. It represents the outcome of long-term interaction between climate, soil, relief, groundwater conditions, and biological processes. Vegetation is one of the strongest indicators of climate and is therefore frequently used in geography to understand environmental regions.

items: Exams frequently ask about the primary factors influencing natural vegetation: climate, soil, relief, groundwater, and biological processes.
Remember that natural vegetation is used in geography as a primary indicator to demarcate climate and environmental regions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Natural vegetation refers to plant life that grows without human aid and remains undisturbed by human activity.
It is the result of long-term interactions between climate, soil, relief, groundwater conditions, and biological processes.
Vegetation acts as one of the strongest indicators of climate in geographic environmental analysis.
